mechanism_narrative: A sustained but slow recovery in workplace mobility over the past two weeks indicates a gradual return to office, which will incrementally boost weekday foot traffic to retail and recreation venues, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES maintaining its current recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week drop in residential mobility indicates a shift in population behavior towards spending less time at home, directly translating to increased out-of-home activities including retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days even if RESIDENTIAL drops by more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent and sustained recovery in both transit station and workplace mobility signifies a broader return to daily commuting and urban activity, creating a synergistic effect that will significantly increase footfall in retail and recreation areas over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing sustained increases for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in parks mobility, likely due to deteriorating weather conditions or increased public health caution, suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure activities. This will reduce overall out-of-home movement and negatively impact incidental retail and recreation visits, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite PARKS mobility continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has been at an extremely suppressed and relatively stable level for the past four weeks, suggesting it has reached a floor. Any future movement is more likely to be a stabilization or a very slight upward adjustment as the market finds its new equilibrium, leading to a slightly higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days declines further by more than 2 percentage points from its current mean.

mechanism_narrative: A significant and sustained increase in grocery and pharmacy mobility indicates a general rise in essential out-of-home trips. This increased comfort and frequency of leaving home will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases by more than 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM showing sustained increases for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in residential mobility and an increase in parks mobility signals a strong behavioral shift towards spending more time outside the home for leisure and recreation. This overall increase in outdoor activity will lead to more incidental retail and recreation visits, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point and PARKS rises by more than 1 point in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL falling and PARKS rising as specified.

mechanism_narrative: If workplace mobility, despite its recent slight recovery, fails to show further sustained increases over the next two weeks, it indicates a stalled return-to-office trend, likely due to a lack of new policy incentives or continued caution. This stagnation in commuting will prevent any significant recovery in RETAIL_REC, leading to lower values over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES does not increase for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases by more than 1 percentage point, despite WORKPLACES failing to show sustained increases.
